course.title: AI Solution Architecture and Platform Design

questions.prompt: Four sentences from the Muyassir notes. Which one is a constraint the design must obey?
options: Cut the median permit cycle from 21 to 10 days
The permits system offers a read interface only this year
Inspectors fear the assistant will sound as if it approves
Most questions are about the same 40 topics
questions.explanation: A constraint is a decision already taken elsewhere. The vendor's read-only interface fixes how Muyassir integrates, whatever the architect prefers.
misconceptions: A goal with a number is a driver: the system exists to reach it, nothing forbids other designs
A worry about behaviour is a concern: it becomes a scenario, not a fixed decision
An unverified belief is an assumption: it must be tested before a design relies on it

questions.prompt: Four drafts for the inspectors' concern. Which one can be tested against pilot data?
options: Muyassir never sounds as if it approves a design
At least 99% of all answers offer a person
At least 99% of approval questions get an offer of a person
The prompt tells the model that only inspectors approve
questions.explanation: It names the slice (approval questions), the metric (offered a person), the statistic (a share) and the target (0.99).
misconceptions: Treats a promise as a target: 'never sounds as if it approves' names no metric or statistic to compute
Measures the wrong population: the share over all questions dilutes the 53 approval questions among 400
Confuses an input with the result: a rule in the prompt is a design choice, not a measured response

questions.prompt: A missing-documents check sends the published building code, an applicant's form with identity number and a site plan to a model. Under the Ministry's rule, where may the model run?
options: In the Ministry or in a cloud region in the Kingdom
Anywhere, since most of the prompt is the published code
Only in the Ministry's own data centre
Anywhere, once the identity number is masked
questions.explanation: The set combines Public and Restricted items, so it is Restricted, which the rule allows in the Ministry and in a cloud region in the Kingdom.
misconceptions: Takes the level of most of the text: the code is the longest part, but the highest level in the set decides
Over-classifies: personal data in a permit form is Restricted here, not Secret
Thinks masking in the prompt changes the level: the site plan and form are still in the set

questions.prompt: The sum of p95s is 4,290 ms: model 2,900, reranker 650, status read 400, the rest 340. Which single change most likely brings the p95 under 4,000 ms without a new model?
options: Write the conversation log faster
Tune the index for a faster median query
Add a second gateway check before the model
Skip reranking for status questions and send fewer clauses
questions.explanation: The reranker's 650 ms and the context size are the levers in the architect's hands, and the sum drops to 3,640 ms; answer quality must then be re-tested.
misconceptions: Optimises a hop that is off the user's path: the log write is asynchronous and adds nothing users wait for
Optimises the p50 instead of the tail: a faster median retrieval moves the p95 sum by tens of milliseconds
Adds a hop for safety without measuring its cost: a second check adds time, it does not remove it

questions.prompt: Day 1 produced a scenario sheet, fourteen classified flows and a request budget. Which finding most limits today's options for Muyassir's answer model?
options: The request costs SAR 0.025, half of its cost target
The reranker takes 650 ms of the p95
Prompts with applicant context are Restricted and stay in the Kingdom
One pilot answer showed another applicant's file
questions.explanation: The level of the prompt removes every option that would send it to an external model; the other findings are fixed inside an option.
misconceptions: Treats a passed scenario as a limit: cost at SAR 0.025 a request leaves room, it rules nothing out
Mistakes a fixable hop for a placement limit: the reranker is a design choice inside every option
Confuses an incident to fix with a constraint on options: P0288 is a defect in the status read

questions.prompt: The reports team wants each report routed to one of six departments, within seconds, at 95,000 reports a month, with 24,000 labelled reports from last year. Which design do you cost first?
options: A classifier trained on the labelled reports
Retrieval over past reports, then a generated answer
An agent that reads the report and calls department tools
A frontier model with a routing prompt
questions.explanation: A label from a fixed list, many labelled examples and a need for speed are the fit questions of the classical pattern.
misconceptions: Uses retrieval for a label: there is no document to cite, only a category to choose
Adds steps a single label does not need: no step depends on another
Reaches for the most capable model before checking the output's shape and the labels

questions.prompt: In Lab 2.2, doubling the token price moves O1's three-year total by 3%, the high forecast by 58%, and O3 loses on unanswered calls. Where should the sponsor's meeting spend its time?
options: Negotiating the token price
Cutting the build cost of O1
Choosing O3 because it is cheapest to run
The volume forecast and how many questions each option answers
questions.explanation: The ranking depends on volume and coverage; the sensitivity table shows it, so the meeting argues about those.
misconceptions: Debates the input with the least effect: the token price barely moves the ranking at this volume
Ignores that build is a small share of three years and similar across options
Treats O3 as cheapest because it is cheapest to run: its unanswered calls dominate

questions.prompt: O1's largest exit factor is its managed vector store with no bulk export (SAR 250,000). Which requirement removes it?
options: The service shall expose an OpenAI-compatible interface
The provider shall export the index, embeddings and metadata in JSON Lines within 10 working days
The contract shall allow exit with 90 days' notice
The provider shall give reasonable help on exit
questions.explanation: The cost is in the data; only an export of the data, in an open format and a set time, removes it.
misconceptions: Moves the calls but not the data: an interface standard leaves the index where it is
Fixes the contract term, not the data: leaving early is cheaper, the index is still stuck
Has no verifiable term: 'reasonable' cannot be checked

questions.prompt: A record chooses to skip the reranker for status questions. Its trigger reads "revisit if quality drops". Which replacement makes it a trigger someone can act on?
options: Revisit when the product owner feels quality has dropped
Revisit every three years
Reopen if Q1 on mixed questions falls below 0.90 on the monthly sample of 200
Reopen if p95 latency rises above 4,000 ms
questions.explanation: The risk the decision took is answer quality on mixed questions; the trigger measures exactly that, with a threshold and a sample.
misconceptions: Keeps the vagueness and adds a person: nobody can tell when quality has dropped
Sets a date with no link to the risk the decision took
Chooses a metric the decision does not affect: latency improved by the change

questions.prompt: Decision record 1 hosts Muyassir's model in a cloud region of the Kingdom. Lab 2.2 found that volume moves the three-year cost by half and token price by 3%. What should its trigger watch first?
options: The provider's token price
Monthly requests, against a threshold below the crossover
The build cost of O1
A single wrong answer reported in the press
questions.explanation: The ranking depends on volume; the trigger fires before the volume at which the Ministry-hosted option catches up.
misconceptions: Watches the input that barely moves the ranking at this volume
Watches a cost already spent: build cannot reopen a hosting decision
Confuses an incident with a decision trigger: one bad answer is a defect to fix

questions.prompt: Only the inspections team uses vision, and its candidate model has no Arabic evaluation. The team asks the platform to offer vision to everyone. What does the platform do first?
options: Build a shared vision service for all nine teams
Refuse, since vision is not in phase 1
Add the vision model to the catalogue now
Give the team a paved road to its own vision service, and ask for Arabic evidence
questions.explanation: One team's need is served by a golden path the team owns; the catalogue waits for the evidence.
misconceptions: Builds from one team's request: shared services carry shared cost and an owner for nine teams
Treats team-owned as unsupported: the team still needs the gateway and a template
Admits a model without the evidence the catalogue requires

questions.prompt: The planning team (Public) labels a request Public and sends it to the external model. The text reads: "Owner 1048837265 asks whether plot 17 can be rezoned."
options: Pass it: the team and the label are both Public
Pass it, and mask the number in the audit log
Refuse it: the content shows an identity number, so the request is Restricted
Pass it with a warning to the team
questions.explanation: The level is the highest the gateway can see; the identity number makes it Restricted, which may not go to an external model.
misconceptions: Trusts the label over the content: labels are what the caller remembered to send
Fixes the data after the fact: masking in the log does not stop the text reaching the model
Moves the risk to the team without stopping it: a warning lets the data out

questions.prompt: The contact team's nightly batch moves to working hours and asks the Ministry-hosted model for more than twice its capacity. Budgets are untouched; the other teams' answers slow down. Which control fixes it?
options: A lower budget on the contact team's key
Revoke the contact team's key
A cap on any team's share of the Ministry-hosted model
Fall back to a cloud model when the queue is long
questions.explanation: The harm is shared capacity; only a cap on each team's share keeps the others served.
misconceptions: Fixes spend, not capacity: the batch runs on a fixed-cost model and spends nothing per call
Treats a legitimate overload as a leak: the key is the team's own and correctly used
Moves the load instead of capping it: the batch spills onto a paid model the other teams share, and only a cloud region in the Kingdom may take its Restricted transcripts

questions.prompt: Priced with the platform's card, August's In-Kingdom Cloud showback is SAR 500 above the invoice. Every token is accounted for. What is the right fix?
options: Add a correction line of SAR -500 to the unallocated bucket
Update the price card for August
Ask teams to tag their calls better
Allocate the invoice lines, the credit included, to the usage they cover
questions.explanation: The invoice holds a credit the card cannot know; allocating the invoice passes it to the teams in proportion to their use.
misconceptions: Hides a gap instead of explaining it: a fudge line makes the next month's gap invisible too
Updates a card that was right: the provider's prices did not change in August
Blames tags for a pricing gap: tags decide who pays, not how much

questions.prompt: Asas moves from one shared key to per-team keys. The planning team's key leaks and calls the external model 400 times a minute. What keeps the other eight teams served?
options: Revoking that team's key when its rate spikes, under per-team budgets
A cap on each team's share of the Ministry-hosted model
A larger shared budget for the hour
A showback that names the planning team
questions.explanation: A per-team key can be revoked without touching anyone else, and a per-team budget bounds the spend until it is.
misconceptions: Contains capacity incidents; the leak spends money on a paid model and takes no shared capacity
Delays the outage: a larger shared pot still runs out for everyone
Decides who pays afterwards; it stops nothing during the hour

questions.prompt: In March the platform adds an Arabic evaluation gate to the template. Services generated after March have it; the reports team's service, generated in January, does not. What went wrong?
options: The reports team should have read the release notes
The template should have had more questions
The service was treated as a one-time copy, with no update path from the template
The gateway should run the evaluation
questions.explanation: A golden path needs a way to bring template changes to services already generated from it.
misconceptions: Blames the team for a platform design gap: nothing told them or carried the change
Makes the template harder to use without fixing older services
Moves a template problem to the gateway, which cannot see a service's evaluation

questions.prompt: The planning team's zoning assistant sends questions about published zoning plans, classified Public, to the external model. A colleague proposes failing every design with an external model, to be safe.
options: Yes: external models are a risk whatever the data
Pass it with a warning that cannot be silenced
Send every external design to the board for review
No: the check enforces the rule by level, and Public data may go to an external host
questions.explanation: A check stricter than the standard blocks allowed work, and teams learn to switch it off.
misconceptions: Treats any external host as a breach: the rule allows Public data anywhere
Ignores that the rule is per level: a warning on every external call trains teams to ignore warnings
Moves the decision to a person on every commit, which is what the check was meant to save

questions.prompt: "A 10% sample review of approved reports is the only check that inspectors' approvals are real." The oversight scenario requires every filed report to carry an approval.
options: Non-compliance
A sensitivity point: whether approvals mean anything rests on that one rate
A non-risk, since every report is approved
A trade-off point
questions.explanation: A sensitivity point is one parameter a scenario depends on; lower the sample rate and rubber-stamping goes unseen.
misconceptions: Reads a weak spot as a broken rule: no standard sets the sample rate
Ignores the dependency: approval is designed in, and its value hangs on one parameter
Needs two attributes moving in opposite directions; this is one parameter under one scenario

questions.prompt: "DR-2026-07: approved. The inspections team may send clean photos to ext-vision-q. Owner: Rabah Al-Mujil. Conditions: the detector runs on every photo; flagged photos stay on the manual path."
options: An expiry, and the events that would bring it back to the board
An owner for the conditions
Any conditions at all
The scope of what is allowed
questions.explanation: Without an expiry and reopen triggers, the exception outlives its reason and becomes the standard.
misconceptions: An owner is named: Rabah Al-Mujil
Conditions are stated, though they need numbers; the larger gap is that nothing ends it
Scope is clear: one team, clean photos, one model

questions.prompt: The sponsor says: run costs for the first year are capped at SAR 1.2 million, the approved budget line. How do you record it?
options: As a driver, with a scenario that measures spend
As a constraint, with the sponsor as its owner
As a concern of the finance and cost lead
As an assumption to test with the pilot
questions.explanation: The cap is a decision already taken that bounds every option; nobody builds the system to spend it.
misconceptions: Treats a limit as a goal: the system does not exist to spend SAR 1.2 million
Mistakes a fixed decision for a worry: the cap is approved, not feared
Confuses an approved budget with a belief: nothing about it needs testing

questions.prompt: Three interviews are done. Which note most deserves a second reading before any design is drawn?
options: The sponsor's target for the permit cycle
The product owner's wish for a dark staff console
The data protection officer's remark that applicant files do not leave the Kingdom
The brief's sentence that the assistant must be fast and accurate
questions.explanation: A placement constraint said in passing rules out whole designs, so it is found before options are drawn.
misconceptions: Thinks drivers rule designs out: a target shapes the options but forbids none
Gives weight to noise: no architecture decision depends on the console colour
Confuses vague targets with constraints: they need numbers, not a second reading

questions.prompt: Which response measure turns the inspectors' concern (only an inspector approves) into a testable scenario?
options: The prompt says that only inspectors approve
Answers never sound like an approval
At least 99% of all answers include a contact number
At least 99% of approval questions receive an offer of a person
questions.explanation: It names the slice, the metric, the statistic and the target, so a reviewer can compute it from logs.
misconceptions: Mistakes a design choice for a measured response
States an intent with no metric or statistic
Measures the wrong population: approval questions are diluted among all answers

questions.prompt: In 400 pilot requests, one answer showed another applicant's deed. Which privacy measure should the scenario use?
options: The number of such answers, with a target of zero
The mean leak rate, with a target below 1%
The p95 of leaks per day
The share of answers that cite a clause
questions.explanation: A single leak is an incident; a sum with a target of zero fails on it, a mean of 0.25% hides it.
misconceptions: Lets a rate hide a harm that counts one by one
Uses a latency statistic for an event count
Measures transparency, not privacy

questions.prompt: A summary job combines published zoning maps with the names and mobile numbers of engineering office contacts. Under the highest-level principle, what is the job's output?
options: Public, because most of it is published
Restricted, because it holds personal data
Secret, because it combines two sources
Unclassified until the job runs
questions.explanation: A set that combines levels takes the highest; contact persons are personal data and Restricted in the case.
misconceptions: Takes the level of the largest part instead of the highest
Thinks combining raises the level by itself
Ignores that data is classified when it is created

questions.prompt: The p95s of the hops of a request add up to 4,290 ms; the end-to-end p95 measured in the pilot is 4,866 ms. What explains the gap?
options: The sum of p95s always overstates, so the measurement is wrong
Retries and queues add time that no single hop's percentile shows
The asynchronous log write was left out of the sum
p50s should have been added instead
questions.explanation: The sum of p95s bounds the hops; retries and queueing between hops add time the per-hop numbers miss.
misconceptions: Trusts the bound over the measurement
Adds a hop users never wait for
A sum of medians understates the tail even more

questions.prompt: Why does the course write the hosting of every container on the container view?
options: So the sponsor sees which vendor was chosen
Because Mermaid requires a hosting label
So a reviewer can check placement against the classified flows by reading the view
Because the context view cannot show external systems
questions.explanation: Hosting on the boxes lets placement be read and diffed with the view.
misconceptions: Mistakes a vendor choice for the placement question
Confuses a course convention with a tool rule
The context view does show external systems

questions.prompt: The inspections team wants its standard letters drafted in the house style from inspector notes; 9,000 approved letters exist. The building code changes monthly. What does fine-tuning give them, and what must still come from elsewhere?
options: Both the style and the current code requirements
The style; the facts come from the inspector's notes
Nothing a prompt cannot give
The current code requirements; the style comes from a template
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning shapes a stable form from many examples; facts that change come from the notes or retrieval.
misconceptions: Thinks tuning keeps knowledge current: the next circular makes a tuned model wrong
Ignores what 9,000 examples make possible; a prompt is a rival to test, not a certainty
Inverts the two: tuning is for form, retrieval for knowledge that changes

questions.prompt: Option O3 has the lowest build and run cost but answers 70% of questions, against 92% for O1. Why can its three-year cost still be the highest?
options: Its build cost is paid every year
Unanswered questions become calls the Ministry also pays for
Non-generative systems need more servers
Its token price is higher
questions.explanation: The cost model counts the calls created by unanswered questions; at 30% unanswered they dominate.
misconceptions: Build is a first-year line only
O3 runs on fixed infrastructure with no capacity units
O3 has no tokens at all

questions.prompt: Doubling the token price moves O1's three-year total by 3%; the high volume forecast moves it by 58%. What belongs in the decision's review trigger?
options: The token price only
A monthly request volume, then the price
The build cost
Nothing: O1 is cheapest
questions.explanation: The ranking depends most on volume, so the trigger watches volume first and price second.
misconceptions: Watches the input with the least effect
Build is spent and cannot reopen the decision
A cheapest option today can stop being cheapest; that is what triggers are for

questions.prompt: With exit cost weighted 0.10, O1 scores 4.20 and O2 4.10; at 0.13, O2 leads. What should the options paper do?
options: Report O1 as the winner and omit the flip
Raise the exit weight until the preferred option wins
Report the ranking and the flip weight, and record the fragility as a bad consequence
Drop weighted scoring from the paper
questions.explanation: Weights are opinions; a close ranking is reported with the weight that reverses it.
misconceptions: Presents an opinion as a fact
Tunes weights to a conclusion
Throws away a useful method instead of reporting its sensitivity

questions.prompt: Which procurement requirement can a reviewer verify?
options: The provider will support a smooth exit
The provider shall make reasonable efforts to export data
The provider shall export all indexed documents in JSON Lines within 10 working days of a request
The provider should prefer open formats
questions.explanation: It uses 'shall', names a format and a time a reviewer can test.
misconceptions: Uses 'will' and no measurable term
Contains an escape phrase
Uses 'should' and no testable term

questions.prompt: The reports team moves routing from its rule list to the classifier one report category at a time, behind its intake endpoint. In week 3, roads reports (30% on the classifier) are correct in 0.895 of 200 graded answers against 0.900 for the rule list, and hand over 0.050 to a person against 0.045. The team advances a category when it is within 0.01 and hands over no more, and rolls back when it is more than 0.02 below. What happens to roads?
options: Move roads to the classifier in full, since the gap is within 0.01
Flip roads back to the rule list
Switch off the rule list for roads
Keep roads at 30% and grade another week
questions.explanation: The quality gap passes but the hand-over share is higher, so neither rule to advance nor rule to roll back is met: hold and keep the way back open.
misconceptions: Reads one of the two conditions: the classifier hands more reports to a person than the rule list
Treats a 0.005 gap as a failure: rolling back is for a gap above 0.02
Retires the legacy path while 70% of roads reports still use it and the rollback is still needed

questions.prompt: Which review trigger can fire?
options: If the situation changes materially
When the team has time to revisit
If monthly requests exceed 600,000 in the gateway logs
When quality seems lower than expected
questions.explanation: It names a measurement, a threshold and where it is measured.
misconceptions: No measurement
No measurement or date
A feeling, not a threshold

questions.prompt: On a shared AI platform, eight of nine teams use or ask for chat and one team asks for speech. How should the platform serve speech?
options: Give the speech team a paved road to a service it owns, behind the gateway
Build a shared speech service for all nine teams first
Refuse speech until more teams ask for it
Let the speech team call any external provider directly
questions.explanation: One team's need is served by a golden path the team owns; shared services are for what most teams need.
misconceptions: Builds a shared service, with shared cost and an owner, for one team
Treats a team-owned capability as unsupported
Bypasses the gateway and its placement policy

questions.prompt: A candidate model tops a public leaderboard, has no evaluation on the Ministry's Arabic set, and its licence forbids production use. What does admission decide?
options: Admit it for Public data only
Reject it on the licence, and ask for Arabic evidence if it is proposed again
Admit it on the leaderboard score and evaluate later
Admit it for a three-month trial in production
questions.explanation: Admission rests on the licence and the Ministry's own evaluations; a leaderboard is neither.
misconceptions: Data level does not cure a licence that forbids production use
Admits without the evidence the catalogue requires
A trial in production is still production use

questions.prompt: A request from a Restricted team declares no classification and names an external model. What should the gateway's policy do?
options: Pass it, since nothing says the data is Restricted
Pass it and log the full prompt for review
Ask the model whether the prompt holds personal data
Treat it as Restricted and refuse it
questions.explanation: An undeclared request takes the team's highest level: the policy fails closed.
misconceptions: Fails open: a missing label is not a Public label
Creates a second copy of possibly Restricted data in the log
Sends the data to the model to decide whether it may be sent

questions.prompt: Why does the gateway's audit log store a hash of each prompt instead of the prompt?
options: Hashes are shorter, so the log is cheaper
The log can prove what was sent without becoming a copy of the data
A hash lets the platform team read the prompt later
Regulators require hashing of all logs
questions.explanation: The log must not hold Restricted text; a hash still proves whether a given text was sent.
misconceptions: Size is a side effect, not the reason
A hash cannot be read back into the text
Invents a requirement; the reason is the data the log would hold

questions.prompt: Under one shared key and budget, a leaked key at one team cuts every team off paid models. Which change contains the leak to that team?
options: A larger shared budget
A cap on each team's share of the Ministry-hosted model
A key and budget per team, with revocation of a key that spikes
A fallback to the Ministry-hosted model
questions.explanation: Per-team keys let one key be revoked without stopping the others; per-key budgets bound the spend.
misconceptions: Only delays the outage
Contains capacity incidents, not spend
Moves the load to a capacity every team shares, and the leaked key keeps working

questions.prompt: A showback priced with the platform's price card is 10.9% above the provider's September invoice after a price cut. What makes the showback reconcile every month?
options: Allocate each invoice line to the usage it covers
Update the price card each quarter
Add the difference to an 'other' line
Ask the teams to tag every call
questions.explanation: Allocating the invoice reproduces what the Ministry pays, including credits and price changes.
misconceptions: Still drifts between updates and misses credits
Hides the gap instead of explaining it
Tags decide who pays, not how much

questions.prompt: The data centre's fixed cost is shared by tokens and the contact team, whose speech model counts many tokens per call, gets 71% of it; by requests it would get 24%. What should the architect do?
options: Use tokens, since it is the default
Use whichever share the contact team accepts
Split the difference at 47%
Choose the key that best tracks server time, measure it, and record the choice
questions.explanation: The allocation key is a decision with consequences; it is measured and recorded, not defaulted.
misconceptions: A default is not a reason
Negotiation is not measurement
Averages two keys without a reason for either

questions.prompt: A platform's service template ships with its evaluation gate switched on. What does that default achieve that a recommendation in the template's README does not?
options: Teams that take the easy way get the gate without deciding to
It makes the gate impossible to switch off
It removes the need for an evaluation set
It moves the evaluation to the gateway
questions.explanation: Most teams keep defaults; a recommendation is what gets skipped under a deadline.
misconceptions: A good default can still be switched off, visibly, with a reason
The gate needs the team's evaluation set to run
The gateway cannot see a service's evaluation

questions.prompt: A team generating a service from the platform's template answers Restricted for its data and an external model for its alias. What should the template do?
options: Generate the service and leave the refusal to the gateway
Refuse at generation, naming the placement rule the answer breaks
Generate the service with the evaluation gate off
Generate the service and email the platform team
questions.explanation: A validator refuses the disallowed placement before any code or data exists.
misconceptions: Lets a non-conforming service be built and deployed first
Switches off an unrelated gate
Notifies without preventing anything

questions.prompt: A design sends Restricted photos to a vision model hosted in the Kingdom, with an external model as its fallback. A placement check looks only at each flow's destination. What happens?
options: The check fails the design, since the fallback is external
The check fails every design that has a fallback
The check passes the design, though Restricted photos reach an external model when the first one fails
The check cannot run on a design with a fallback
questions.explanation: A fallback is a second destination for the same data; a check must follow it to see it.
misconceptions: Credits the check with reading fallbacks it ignores
Over-reaches: fallbacks within the rule are fine
The check runs; it just checks too little

questions.prompt: A pipeline runs test, deploy, then a non-blocking evaluate stage with a 0.85 threshold on Arabic and English sets. Does it meet a standard that asks for an evaluation gate?
options: Yes: it has an evaluate stage with a threshold
Yes, if the threshold is raised to 0.90
No: it needs a third language set
No: an evaluation after deployment that blocks nothing gates nothing
questions.explanation: A gate must block, and before deployment; otherwise users already have the release it measures.
misconceptions: Reads the stage's name, not its order or effect
The threshold is not the problem
Language coverage is not the problem here

questions.prompt: A weekly comparison of Asas's declared settings with the running gateway finds the contracts team's rate limit at 90 calls a minute; the reviewed file says 60. The change was made by hand in a deadline week, under an emergency ticket the platform owner approved. What should the platform team do now?
options: Write 90 into the declared file through a reviewed change, then apply it
Apply the declared file again, so the limit returns to 60
Leave it: the approved ticket is the record of the change
Raise every team's limit by hand so the platform stays consistent
questions.explanation: An approved hand change is brought into the code through review; then the declared file and the running gateway agree again and the checks read the truth.
misconceptions: Reverts an approved change and cuts the team back mid-deadline: revert is for changes nobody approved
Leaves the drift in place: the next apply of the declared file silently undoes the change
Answers drift with more hand changes, none reviewed and none in the file

questions.prompt: In a review, the board notes: 'The vision call takes 3,800 ms of the 5,000 ms latency budget.' How should it be tagged?
options: A sensitivity point: the latency scenario depends on that one parameter
Non-compliance: the budget is nearly spent
A trade-off point: latency against quality
A non-risk: the budget is met
questions.explanation: One parameter decides whether a scenario is met; whether it becomes a risk depends on how much it moves.
misconceptions: No written standard is broken
Names no decision that moves two attributes in opposite directions
Misses how little room is left

questions.prompt: A review has an hour. Which scenario should it examine first?
options: Oversight: important, easy to meet
Arabic answer quality: important, hard to meet
Latency: of medium importance, hard to meet
Operability: of low importance, of medium difficulty
questions.explanation: A utility tree leads with scenarios high in both importance and difficulty.
misconceptions: Important but easy: little for the review to find
Hard, but less important than an important and hard scenario
Least important

questions.prompt: A deviation lets a team send photos the on-device detector passes as clean to an external model. Which record is complete?
options: Approved; owner named; conditions listed
Approved for as long as the team needs it, with conditions
Approved with conditions that carry numbers, the residual risk and who accepts it, an expiry date and reopen triggers
Refused, because any risk is too much
questions.explanation: A deviation is bounded: verifiable conditions, a stated residual, an owner of that risk and an end.
misconceptions: Has no expiry or residual risk
Has no end: it becomes the standard
Refusing has a cost too, and the record must state it
